hook.text: The word 'propaganda' was coined by the Catholic Church in 1622 to spread the faith.

buildup.text: Originally neutral, it just meant spreading ideas. Over time, it gained sinister connotations.

discovery.text: Propaganda is communication designed to influence attitudes using emotional rather than rational appeals.

twist.text: All propaganda is persuasion, but not all persuasion is propaganda. The line is intention and deception.

climax.text: Understanding propaganda starts with admitting that we're all susceptible to it.

punchline.text: Propaganda works best on those who think it doesn't.

quiz.question: What distinguishes propaganda from ordinary persuasion?
options: It relies on emotional appeals and often deception
